assistant_message:
Yes, I would add it, but I would treat it as a simple continuity pilot after install, not as a big new service line yet.

Your current model already has strong front-end economics: $1,000 CAC, about $10,000 first-30-day gross profit, and 1.0-month payback, so the maintenance offer is not needed to fix acquisition. Its job is to improve the back end: continuity offers are for ongoing value with ongoing payments, and they stabilize cash flow while increasing profit per customer [continuity-offers:0]. In the four-offer stack, continuity is specifically the back-end recurring cash-flow layer, while the framework also warns to add layers deliberately and keep as few offers as possible to avoid operational drag [offer-types:4].

For this design business, I would test a post-install Owner Care plan for STR and second-home owners: seasonal refresh guidance, vendor coordination, replacement sourcing, listing/photo review, and priority access before peak season. Price it monthly or quarterly, keep fulfillment lightweight, and make the first version available only to completed install clients.

I would not sell it as "maintenance for maintenance's sake." The better pitch is the valuable bonus or outcome: keeping the property guest-ready, photo-ready, and protected from design decay. That matches the continuity-bonus idea: get customers into continuity with a soft pitch after the main cash offers, then optional prepayment can add more first-30-day cash once the offer proves retention [continuity-bonus:3].

My next move would be a capped pilot: offer it to the next 5 to 10 install clients, track attach rate, monthly gross profit, hours required, and cancellations after 90 days. If it stays high-margin and low-touch, then it improves the money model by adding recurring gross profit without weakening the already-good install economics.
